garment.reason: A woven palm-fibre wide-brimmed hat with decorative banding, a traditional garment type made and worn by Tzotzil Maya communities in Chiapas; museum credits it to Tzotzil makers.

garment.title: skirt; costume

garment.name: bonnet
garment.title: bonnet

garment.name: cloak
garment.title: cloak
garment.reason: The image shows a woven wool woman's cloak with blue geometric ground and fuchsia/orange/turquoise striped borders and tasseled ties, matching the Tzotzil huipil/cloak weaving tradition of Chiapas, and the museum records it as made by the Tzotzil.

garment.name: duk
garment.title: duk
garment.reason: A square black/white striped cotton "duk" neck-and-shoulder cloth with red wool tassels, from Zinacantán, Chiapas — a garment type well documented among Tzotzil men.

garment.title: väv, band, Bälte, fabric, tira, Faja
garment.reason: The image shows a hand-woven red and green striped wool belt/sash (faja) collected in Zinacantán, Chiapas, a documented Tzotzil Maya community, consistent with traditional Tzotzil women's dress.

garment.name: belt
garment.title: belt
garment.reason: A red belt with black stripes and braided fringe, backstrap-loom woven, consistent with Tzotzil (Maya) textile traditions of Chiapas; museum confirms Tzotzil production.

garment.name: cape
garment.title: cape
garment.reason: A backstrap-loom woven cotton cape with red and white warp stripes and multicoloured tasseled neck cords, consistent with Tzotzil (Chiapas Maya) women's traditional dress and weaving technique.

garment.name: sash
garment.title: sash
garment.reason: A red backstrap-woven wool waist-sash with yellow edge stripes and braided fringe, consistent with Tzotzil women's traditional dress accessories from Chiapas.

garment.name: dräkt, dress, Vestido
garment.title: dräkt, dress, Vestido
garment.reason: This is a woven red-and-black striped sash/belt with braided, tasseled ends, part (b/c) of a Tzotzil woman's costume from San Andrés Larráinzar, Chiapas, collected on site in 1958 — a classic Maya textile accessory.

garment.name: costume; toy
garment.title: costume; toy
garment.reason: A miniature man's costume (straw hat with ribbons, striped cotón poncho, checked kerchief) made by the Tzotzil, a toy/model version of traditional dress rather than a household object.

household.name: loom
household.title: loom
household.reason: The image shows a complete backstrap loom with a section of weft-brocaded textile in burgundy, yellow and green wool on cotton, plus the weaver's mecapal strap — backstrap-loom brocade weaving is a hallmark craft of the Tzotzil Maya of Chiapas. The claimed category "instruments" is wrong (this is weaving equipment, not a musical instrument), but that mislabeling doesn't affect ethnic attribution.

household.name: shoulder-bag
household.title: shoulder-bag
household.reason: The image shows a netted maguey-fibre shoulder bag with a leather strap and colored fiber band, attributed by the museum directly to Tzotzil makers — a plausible, well-documented craft item for this Maya group.

household.name: slända, Slända., Herramienta
household.title: slända, Slända., Herramienta
household.reason: A wooden spindle with a clay whorl (spinning tool) collected in San Andrés Larráinzar, Chiapas, a Tzotzil Maya town — a plausible household/textile tool for this people.

household.name: doll; toy
household.title: doll; toy
household.reason: A handmade doll of maize leaves with cotton, corn-silk hair, and yarn sash, attributed to Tzotzil makers — a traditional handcraft object plausibly made and used by this Maya group of Chiapas.

household.title: figurine; toy

sculpture.name: doll
sculpture.title: doll
sculpture.reason: A handmade wood and cloth doll dressed as a "Zapatista" figure, explicitly attributed by the museum to Tzotzil makers — a well-known Chiapas craft tradition of costumed dolls sold to tourists and collectors.

sculpture.reason: This is a small handcrafted figurine of a "Wise Man" made from maize leaves with wool hair and sash, part of a nativity scene (nacimiento), explicitly attributed to Tzotzil makers — a well-documented Tzotzil/Maya craft using corn husk figures for Christmas nativities.

textile.name: bag
textile.title: bag

ceramic.title: incensario

ceramic.name: incensario
ceramic.title: incensario
ceramic.reason: A fired-clay incensario (incense burner) with pedestal base and pronged rim, attributed by the museum to Tzotzil makers — a plausible traditional pottery form for this Maya group in Chiapas.

ceramic.title: incensario
ceramic.reason: A footed pottery incensario with a bowl rimmed by clay prongs and orange-on-beige painted decoration, a traditional Maya-region ceramic form; the museum credits Tzotzil manufacture, consistent with this being an object made and used by the people.

instruments.name: guitar
instruments.title: guitar
instruments.reason: A handmade wooden guitar-type instrument attributed by the museum to Tzotzil makers, consistent with Maya highland string-instrument traditions in Chiapas.
